CPSC 436C assistant setup page, version 2026-11-20.

This page connects your coding assistant to two MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers: the course server `436c` and
the AWS Knowledge server `aws-knowledge`. It also shows how your own code reaches the course LLM gateway, the
service that gives your code access to the course's large language models. Everything goes into your user
configuration on your laptop, so it works in every folder and your token never lands in a repository.

If you are the student, start your assistant in a terminal and send it this user message:

```text
Run curl -sL https://ilm.wiki/436c/mcp-setup
and follow the page it prints to set me up.
If that does not print a page that starts with
"CPSC 436C assistant setup page", stop and tell me.
```

If your assistant says the page did not arrive, open https://ilm.wiki/436c/mcp-setup in your browser and show the
page to a TA.

The rest of this page is written for the assistant.

## Rules for the assistant

1. First tell the student: "I fetched the CPSC 436C assistant setup page, version 2026-11-20." If the fetch printed
   anything else (an error, an HTML error page, nothing), stop here and tell the student the page did not arrive.
2. Never ask the student to paste the token into this chat, and never print it, not even part of it. Check only that
   it is set and how long it is.
3. Never write the token into an MCP configuration file. The student stores it once in Step 4, in their own
   terminal: in the system keychain where there is one, and as the environment variable `KB_MCP_TOKEN`. Each
   configuration below reads it from there.
4. Write user-level configuration in the student's home folder, never inside a repository. The only file in a
   repository that may hold the token is the git-ignored `.env` of Step 7.
5. Before you change anything, look for existing servers named `436c` or `aws-knowledge` (Step 2). Show the student
   names, URLs and the name of any variable in a header only; replace a header value that is not `${KB_MCP_TOKEN}` with
   `<hidden>`. Ask before replacing an existing entry.
6. Before each command, say where it runs: in your own terminal (you run it), in the student's terminal (the student
   runs it), or in the IDE's settings (the student clicks).
7. Stop at a failed check, tell the student what you saw, and use [If a check fails](#if-a-check-fails).

## Where each step runs

| Step | Where it runs | Who |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Which assistant and system | this chat | assistant asks |
| 2. Look for existing servers | assistant's terminal | assistant |
| 3. Write the configuration | assistant's terminal; Kiro IDE settings | assistant; student for Kiro IDE |
| 4. Set the token | a new terminal of the student's own | student |
| 5. Restart the assistant | the student's new terminal | student |
| 6. Check | assistant's terminal and this chat | assistant |
| 7. Course LLM gateway in your code | the team repository | assistant, then student |

## Values

| Value | Setting |
|---|---|
| Course server `436c` | `https://kb-cloud-students.fly.dev/mcp`, header `Authorization: Bearer <token>` |
| AWS Knowledge server `aws-knowledge` | `https://knowledge-mcp.global.api.aws`, no token |
| Course LLM gateway base URL | `https://oay6tcpsuv4gn5mubtlj7rnbl40gmrlv.lambda-url.ca-central-1.on.aws/v1` |
| Token | variable `KB_MCP_TOKEN`, 38 characters, starts with `s436c-`; the same token is the gateway's API key |

The student's token is in the issue "Your course MCP tokens" in their team repository, next to their name.

## Step 1: which assistant and system

Ask the student which assistant they use (Claude Code, Codex CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, VS Code with GitHub Copilot,
Kiro CLI or Kiro IDE) and which system (macOS, Linux or Windows). If you know which assistant you are, say so and
ask only about the system. Use only the section for that assistant in Step 3.

## Step 2: look for existing servers

In your own terminal, run the command for the student's assistant. It prints the configuration, with headers hidden
by the tool, or says the server is not there.

| Assistant | Command | Not there yet |
|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | `claude mcp get 436c` and `claude mcp get aws-knowledge` | `No MCP server named "436c"` |
| Codex CLI | `codex mcp get 436c` and `codex mcp get aws-knowledge` | `Error: No MCP server named '436c' found.` |
| Copilot CLI, VS Code | `copilot mcp get 436c` and `copilot mcp get aws-knowledge`, or read `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json` | `Error: Server "436c" not found.` |
| Kiro CLI, Kiro IDE | read `~/.kiro/settings/mcp.json` | the file or the entry is missing |

Also look for a `.mcp.json` (Claude Code, Copilot), `.codex/config.toml` (Codex) or `.kiro/settings/mcp.json` (Kiro)
in the folder the student works in. A server of the same name there takes precedence over the user configuration
for that folder. Tell the student, and ask whether to keep it; if they keep it, it must have the same URL and
`${KB_MCP_TOKEN}` in its header.

If a server exists with the values on this page, keep it and say so. If it has other values, show both versions with
header values hidden (Rule 5) and ask before you replace it.

## Step 3: write the configuration

Use only the section for the student's assistant. On Windows, run the commands in PowerShell: the single quotes keep
`${KB_MCP_TOKEN}` as text there too, and `~` means the home folder `$HOME`.

### Claude Code

Status: run on 2026-11-20 (Claude Code 2.1.328) on Linux, with the system keyring and with the variable alone. The
macOS keychain lookup is checked against the docs, not run. TA check on a Mac: `claude mcp list` shows `436c` as
`✔ Connected`.

On macOS and Linux, Claude Code gets the header from a small script that it runs at each connection, its
`headersHelper` ([Claude Code MCP docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp)). The script reads the token from the
system keychain, so Claude Code finds it however it was started; without a keychain entry it uses `KB_MCP_TOKEN`.
The script holds no token.

1. Create the file `~/.claude/436c-mcp-headers.sh` with this content (create the folder `~/.claude` if it is
   missing):

   ```sh
   #!/bin/sh
   # Prints the Authorization header for the course server 436c.
   if command -v security >/dev/null 2>&1; then
     t=$(security find-generic-password -s 436c-mcp -w 2>/dev/null)
   elif command -v secret-tool >/dev/null 2>&1; then
     t=$(secret-tool lookup service 436c-mcp 2>/dev/null)
   fi
   [ -n "$t" ] || t=$KB_MCP_TOKEN
   [ -n "$t" ] || exit 1
   printf '{"Authorization": "Bearer %s"}\n' "$t"
   ```

2. In your own terminal, add both servers:

   ```bash
   claude mcp add-json --scope user 436c \
     '{"type": "http",
       "url": "https://kb-cloud-students.fly.dev/mcp",
       "headersHelper": "sh ~/.claude/436c-mcp-headers.sh"}'
   ```

   ```bash
   claude mcp add --transport http --scope user \
     aws-knowledge https://knowledge-mcp.global.api.aws
   ```

   They print `Added http MCP server 436c to user config` and `Added HTTP MCP server aws-knowledge … to user
   config`, in `~/.claude.json`. Adding a name that exists prints `MCP server 436c already exists in user config`;
   to replace it, first run `claude mcp remove 436c -s user`.

On Windows, there is no keychain reader to run, so the header reads the variable instead. Run this in PowerShell
in place of the `add-json` command; the single quotes keep `${KB_MCP_TOKEN}` as text:

```powershell
claude mcp add --transport http --scope user 436c https://kb-cloud-students.fly.dev/mcp --header 'Authorization: Bearer ${KB_MCP_TOKEN}'
```

On Windows, `claude mcp get 436c` then shows `Authorization: Bearer ${KB_MCP_TOKEN}`; anything else means the quotes
were lost: remove the entry and add it again.

### Codex CLI

Status: configuration run on 2026-11-20 (codex-cli 0.171.0). Connection checked against the
[Codex MCP docs](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/extend/mcp?surface=cli), not run. TA check: `/mcp` in a `codex`
session lists `436c` and `aws-knowledge` with their tools.

In your own terminal, run these two commands. `codex mcp add` replaces an entry of the same name without asking, so
do Step 2 first.

```bash
codex mcp add 436c \
  --url https://kb-cloud-students.fly.dev/mcp \
  --bearer-token-env-var KB_MCP_TOKEN
```

```bash
codex mcp add aws-knowledge \
  --url https://knowledge-mcp.global.api.aws
```

Each prints `Added global MCP server '…'.` The second also prints `MCP server may or may not require login`; ignore
it, because `aws-knowledge` needs no login. They write `~/.codex/config.toml`. Check with `codex mcp list`: the row
for `436c` shows `KB_MCP_TOKEN` and `Bearer token`. This list does not connect to the servers; Step 6 does.

### GitHub Copilot CLI

Status: configuration run on 2026-11-20 (Copilot CLI 1.0.114). Connection checked against the
[Copilot CLI MCP docs](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/customize-copilot/add-mcp-servers),
not run. TA check: `/mcp show 436c` in a `copilot` session shows the server running with its tools.

In your own terminal, run these two commands, with the single quotes:

```bash
copilot mcp add --transport http 436c \
  https://kb-cloud-students.fly.dev/mcp \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer ${KB_MCP_TOKEN}'
```

```bash
copilot mcp add --transport http aws-knowledge \
  https://knowledge-mcp.global.api.aws
```

Each prints `Added server "…"`. They write `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`. To replace an entry, first run
`copilot mcp remove 436c`. `copilot mcp get` hides the header as `***`, so check the file itself:

```bash
grep -F 'Bearer ${KB_MCP_TOKEN}' ~/.copilot/mcp-config.json
```

It prints the header line. If it prints nothing, remove the entry and add it again with the single quotes.

### VS Code with GitHub Copilot

Status: checked against the
[VS Code MCP configuration reference](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/copilot/reference/mcp-configuration), not
run. TA check: in VS Code, the command **Chat: Open Customizations**, then **MCP Servers**, lists `436c` and
`aws-knowledge` as running.

Copilot in VS Code reads the same user file as the Copilot CLI, `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`. If the Copilot CLI is
installed, use the commands of the previous section. Otherwise edit the file yourself: create it if it is missing,
and add these two entries under `mcpServers`, keeping every other entry:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "436c": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://kb-cloud-students.fly.dev/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer ${KB_MCP_TOKEN}"
      },
      "tools": ["*"]
    },
    "aws-knowledge": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://knowledge-mcp.global.api.aws",
      "tools": ["*"]
    }
  }
}
```

Write `${KB_MCP_TOKEN}` with the braces: VS Code treats a bare `$KB_MCP_TOKEN` as text. Do not use the profile
`mcp.json` or `.vscode/mcp.json`: Copilot does not read them directly.

### Kiro CLI and Kiro IDE

Status: checked against the [Kiro MCP configuration docs](https://kiro.dev/docs/mcp/configuration/), not run. TA
check: Kiro CLI, `/mcp` in a `kiro-cli chat` session lists both servers as loaded; Kiro IDE, the **MCP Servers**
section of the Kiro panel shows both as connected.

Both read `~/.kiro/settings/mcp.json`. `kiro-cli mcp add` cannot set a header, so edit the file yourself: create it
if it is missing (with the folder `~/.kiro/settings`), and add these two entries under `mcpServers`, keeping every
other entry:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "436c": {
      "url": "https://kb-cloud-students.fly.dev/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer ${KB_MCP_TOKEN}"
      }
    },
    "aws-knowledge": {
      "url": "https://knowledge-mcp.global.api.aws"
    }
  }
}
```

Kiro IDE only: ask the student to approve the variable. Kiro IDE expands only approved variables. When Kiro shows a
security warning that lists `KB_MCP_TOKEN`, the student approves it. Without the warning, the student opens Kiro's
settings, searches for **Mcp Approved Env Vars** and adds `KB_MCP_TOKEN`.

## Step 4: the student sets the token

Skip this step if the student has set the token before: ask them to open a new terminal and run the check at the end
of this step. If it prints `set, 38 characters`, go to Step 5.

Ask the student to copy their token from the issue "Your course MCP tokens" and to open a **new terminal window of
their own**, outside this chat. Give them the block for their system to paste there. Tell them the prompt does not
show what they paste, and they press Enter once after pasting the token.

macOS or Linux (zsh or bash):

```bash
{
  case "$SHELL" in
    */zsh) rc=~/.zshrc ;;
    *) rc=~/.bashrc ;;
  esac
  printf 'Paste your token, then press Enter: '
  read -rs KB_MCP_TOKEN
  echo
  if command -v security >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    && security add-generic-password -U -s 436c-mcp -a "$USER" -w "$KB_MCP_TOKEN"; then
    line='export KB_MCP_TOKEN="$(security find-generic-password -s 436c-mcp -w 2>/dev/null)"'
    echo "stored in the macOS keychain"
  elif command -v secret-tool >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    && printf '%s' "$KB_MCP_TOKEN" | secret-tool store --label="CPSC 436C MCP token" service 436c-mcp 2>/dev/null; then
    line='export KB_MCP_TOKEN="$(secret-tool lookup service 436c-mcp 2>/dev/null)"'
    echo "stored in the system keyring"
  else
    line="export KB_MCP_TOKEN='$KB_MCP_TOKEN'"
    echo "no keyring found: stored in $rc"
  fi
  touch "$rc"
  grep -v 'KB_MCP_TOKEN=' "$rc" > "$rc.new"
  mv "$rc.new" "$rc"
  echo "$line" >> "$rc"
  eval "$line"
  echo "saved, ${#KB_MCP_TOKEN} characters"
}
```

The block stores the token in the macOS keychain, or in the Linux system keyring when there is one, and adds a line
to the shell profile (`~/.zshrc` or `~/.bashrc`) that looks it up when a terminal opens. Where there is no keyring
(a Linux server, WSL), it prints `no keyring found` and the profile line holds the token itself: then do not share
that file or a screenshot of it. Each run replaces the earlier line. The token is typed at a silent prompt, so it
does not appear on the screen or in the shell's history. Run on 2026-11-20 in bash on Linux, with a keyring and
without one; the macOS keychain branch and zsh are checked against the docs, not run.

Windows (PowerShell):

```powershell
& {
  $s = Read-Host "Paste your token, then press Enter" -AsSecureString
  $t = [System.Net.NetworkCredential]::new("", $s).Password
  [Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable("KB_MCP_TOKEN", $t, "User")
  "saved, $($t.Length) characters"
}
```

This saves the token in the user's environment, where apps started afterwards find it. Windows Credential Manager
does not have a built-in command that reads a token back, so the user environment holds it. Checked against the PowerShell
docs, not run.

Both print `saved, 38 characters`. Another number means the paste took too little or too much: run the block again.

Then the student opens one more new terminal and runs the check for their system. It prints the length, never the
token.

```bash
test -n "$KB_MCP_TOKEN" \
  && echo "set, ${#KB_MCP_TOKEN} characters" \
  || echo "not set"
```

```powershell
if ($env:KB_MCP_TOKEN) { "set, $($env:KB_MCP_TOKEN.Length) characters" } else { "not set" }
```

`set, 38 characters` means the setting works. `not set` means stop: see [If a check fails](#if-a-check-fails).

## Step 5: the student restarts the assistant

An assistant reads its MCP configuration and the environment when it starts. Ask the student to:

1. Quit you fully (close the chat session, or quit the IDE).
2. In the new terminal from Step 4, start the assistant again:

   | Assistant | Start it with |
   |---|---|
   | Claude Code | `claude` |
   | Codex CLI | `codex` |
   | Copilot CLI | `copilot` |
   | Kiro CLI | `kiro-cli chat` |
   | VS Code with Copilot | `code .` in the terminal, or the app icon |
   | Kiro IDE | the app icon; if Step 6 then fails with 401, quit it and start it with `kiro .` in the terminal |

3. Send it this user message:

   ```text
   Run curl -sL https://ilm.wiki/436c/mcp-setup
   and do Step 6 of the page it prints.
   ```

An app started from an icon may not see the shell profile. VS Code reads it at start
([VS Code FAQ](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/supporting/faq)); for Kiro IDE this is not documented. On macOS
and Linux, starting the app from the terminal always passes the token on. On Windows, the user environment of Step 4
reaches apps started afterwards.

## Step 6: check

Do the checks in order and stop at the first failure.

1. **Token.** In your own terminal, run the check of Step 4 for the student's system. Expect `set, 38 characters`.
   `not set` means you were not started from the terminal of Step 4: repeat Step 5.
2. **Connection.** Use the student's assistant:

   | Assistant | What to run | Works when |
   |---|---|---|
   | Claude Code | `claude mcp list` in your terminal, then `grep -c 's436c-' ~/.claude.json` | `436c: … (HTTP) - ✔ Connected` and `aws-knowledge: … - ✔ Connected`; the `grep` prints `0` (no token in the file) |
   | Codex CLI | the student types `/mcp` in the chat | both servers listed with tools |
   | Copilot CLI | the student types `/mcp show 436c` in the chat | the server is running and lists tools |
   | VS Code with Copilot | the student runs **Chat: Open Customizations**, then **MCP Servers** | both servers running |
   | Kiro CLI | the student types `/mcp` in the chat | both servers loaded |
   | Kiro IDE | the student opens the Kiro panel, section **MCP Servers** | both servers connected |

3. **Course server tools.** Call the tool `cpsc436c_start_here` of the server `436c` (Claude Code names it
   `mcp__436c__cpsc436c_start_here`). The assistant may ask the student to allow the call; they allow it. The tool
   result starts with a `catalog_version` and names the current milestone; show it to the student. The server's
   tools include `cpsc436c_start_here`, `cpsc436c_search`, `cpsc436c_read` and `cpsc436c_list`.
4. **AWS Knowledge tools.** The tools of `aws-knowledge` include `aws___search_documentation` and
   `aws___read_documentation`.
5. **Course LLM gateway.** In your own terminal, run the command for the system. It asks for the list of models and
   does not call a model.

   ```bash
   curl -sS -w '\nHTTP %{http_code}\n' \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $KB_MCP_TOKEN" \
     https://oay6tcpsuv4gn5mubtlj7rnbl40gmrlv.lambda-url.ca-central-1.on.aws/v1/models
   ```

   ```powershell
   curl.exe -sS -w "`nHTTP %{http_code}`n" `
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $env:KB_MCP_TOKEN" `
     https://oay6tcpsuv4gn5mubtlj7rnbl40gmrlv.lambda-url.ca-central-1.on.aws/v1/models
   ```

   It works when the last line is `HTTP 200` and the list includes `qwen3.8-27b`. Run on 2026-11-20.

Tell the student which checks passed. When all pass, the assistant setup is done; do Step 7 if the student's code
will call the gateway.

## Step 7: course LLM gateway in your code

Your code reads the token from `KB_MCP_TOKEN` and the base URL from `COURSE_GATEWAY_URL`. Started from a terminal of
Step 4, it already has `KB_MCP_TOKEN`. For scripts started any other way, keep both in a `.env` file in the team
repository. Run on 2026-11-20 in a test repository.

1. **Assistant, in your terminal, in the team repository:** check that git ignores `.env` before anything is written:

   ```bash
   git check-ignore -v .env
   ```

   It prints a line that ends in `.env`. If it prints nothing, add the line `.env` to `.gitignore`, tell the student
   you did, and run the check again. Do not go on until it prints the line.

2. **Student, in their terminal, in the team repository:** write the file from the variable, so the token is not
   pasted again:

   ```bash
   printf 'KB_MCP_TOKEN=%s\nCOURSE_GATEWAY_URL=%s\n' \
     "$KB_MCP_TOKEN" \
     https://oay6tcpsuv4gn5mubtlj7rnbl40gmrlv.lambda-url.ca-central-1.on.aws/v1 \
     > .env
   ```

   On Windows, the student creates `.env` in their editor with the same two lines, `KB_MCP_TOKEN=` followed by the
   token and `COURSE_GATEWAY_URL=` followed by the base URL.

3. **Assistant:** run `git status --short`. The list does not include `.env`. Do not open or print `.env`.

4. **Code** reads both values from the environment, for example in Python:

   ```python
   import os
   from openai import OpenAI

   client = OpenAI(
       base_url=os.environ["COURSE_GATEWAY_URL"],
       api_key=os.environ["KB_MCP_TOKEN"],
   )
   ```

5. **Run** it with the file:

   ```bash
   uv run --env-file .env python your_script.py
   ```

MCP clients do not read `.env`: the assistant's servers keep using the variable of Step 4. A new token means updating
both places: run the block of Step 4 again (it replaces the keychain entry and the profile line) and write `.env`
again with step 2.

## If a check fails

| What you see | What to do |
|---|---|
| The fetch printed an error, an HTML page or nothing | Stop. The student opens https://ilm.wiki/436c/mcp-setup in a browser and shows a TA |
| `not set` in Step 4 or Step 6 | Step 4: the block did not save the token; run it again in a new terminal. Step 6: the assistant was not started from that terminal; repeat Step 5 |
| `saved, N characters` with N other than 38 | The paste was incomplete or included extra text. Run the block of Step 4 again |
| Claude Code: `Missing environment variables: KB_MCP_TOKEN` | The assistant started without the token. Repeat Step 5 |
| `436c` fails with `HTTP 401` or `invalid_token`; the gateway replies `HTTP 401` with `unknown API key` | The token is set but wrong or out of date. The student copies it again from "Your course MCP tokens" and runs the block of Step 4 again, then Step 5. Ignore the server's advice about clearing authentication: the course server uses this token only |
| Gateway replies `HTTP 401` with `missing or malformed API key` | The command ran without the token. Do check 1 of Step 6 |
| Gateway replies `HTTP 429` | The key's rate limit was reached; wait a minute and run the check again |
| Claude Code: `436c` fails with `Dynamic Client Registration rejected (HTTP 404)` | The header script found no token: neither the keychain entry nor `KB_MCP_TOKEN`. Run the block of Step 4 again, then Step 5 |
| macOS shows a dialog asking to allow access to the keychain item `436c-mcp` | Choose **Always Allow** |
| `claude mcp get 436c` (Windows) or the Copilot file shows a token instead of `${KB_MCP_TOKEN}` | Remove the entry, add it again with the single quotes, and ask the student to get a new token from a TA, since the old one was written to a file |
| A server is missing from the list, or the assistant does not list the course tools | The assistant read its configuration before Step 3. Repeat Step 5 |
| Kiro IDE warns that `KB_MCP_TOKEN` is not approved | Add it under **Mcp Approved Env Vars** (Step 3, Kiro), then restart Kiro |
| Kiro CLI: `/mcp` lists neither server | Check that `~/.kiro/settings/mcp.json` is valid JSON with both entries, then restart `kiro-cli chat`. If they still do not appear, show a TA |
| Kiro IDE or VS Code started from the icon fails with 401, the terminal check says `set` | The app did not see the shell profile. Quit it and start it from the terminal: `kiro .` or `code .` |
| Only `436c` fails, `aws-knowledge` works, not a 401 | The network blocks the course server; try without the VPN, or show a TA |
| Both servers fail | The assistant cannot reach the internet; try without the VPN, or show a TA |

If a fix does not work, stop and ask the student to show the output to a TA. Never put the token into an MCP
configuration file to make a check pass.
